public_rationale: There were concrete exit signs before the post: Anthropic had submitted IPO paperwork and Cerebras had begun public trading. These materially challenge the sweeping pessimism. However, few does not mean none. The available aggregate venture data also warn that headline exit activity was concentrated. Without an AI-specific comparison population, these examples do not settle whether credible exit prospects were scarce across the sector or justify a conclusion about every investor.
limitations: IPO preparation does not guarantee a listing or investor profit.
Cerebras is directly relevant to the broad AI reading, but less so if these companies means only frontier labs.
Overall venture exit totals cannot substitute for AI-specific evidence.
The period choice excludes later developments from outcome evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There are few signs that VC-backed AI companies can be sold to anyone or taken public, so every VC invested in AI needs a miracle.

statement.excerpt: And every VC invested in AI needs a miracle, because there are few signs that these companies can be sold to anyone or taken public.

from_speaker: these companies can be sold to anyone or taken public
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that credible acquisition and IPO prospects are scarce across VC-backed AI companies.
Needs a miracle expresses the claimed severity of the exit problem; it is not treated as a literal supernatural prediction or a specified investment-return threshold.
The broad phrase every VC invested in AI includes AI infrastructure and application companies, while the surrounding discussion also makes frontier labs relevant.
Because this describes an ongoing market state without a period, use April through June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter reportable before the August 11 post.
An IPO filing is a sign of a possible exit, not proof of a completed listing or investor profit. A few examples cannot by themselves disprove few signs.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence for the target quarter shows scarce credible acquisition and IPO routes across VC-backed AI companies, with sufficiently broad difficulty to substantiate the sweeping inference about their investors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows sufficiently widespread credible acquisition or IPO routes to defeat the asserted scarcity and its sweeping inference. Completed listings and announced transactions count, but funding rounds alone do not.
